subject: Post-incident technical brief and action handoff — PaymentsPlus
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@paymentsplus.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident technical brief and action handoff — PaymentsPlus

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated Friday's inference degradation in your Dedicated pool. Attached is a concise technical brief (rca_paymentsplus_20261201.pdf) that summarizes the incident timeline, root cause, and our corrective/remediation plan. High-level summary below: 

- Impact: elevated token latency and occasional 5xx errors for ~45 minutes (2026-11-27 18:03–18:48 UTC).
- Root cause: an interaction between a GPU driver timeout regression and our KV-cache eviction logic that caused the serving runtime to deschedule active async token flushes under high seqlen tails.
- Immediate mitigations applied: rolled a conservative driver runtime flag and reverted a recent KV-cache aggressiveness change (completed within 25 minutes of detection).
- Next steps: validated temporary mitigations in your pool; deploying a targeted runtime patch this week and a kernel-driver patch next week.

Action items for PaymentsPlus: please confirm a 30-minute verification window (proposed: Thu 2026-12-03 10:00–10:30 PST) so we can run load checks from your side and ours. We will share the live diagnostic dashboard during the call.

Attachments: rca_paymentsplus_20261201.pdf (summary + timeline), kernel_patch_notes.txt (technical patch notes), mitigation_playbook.md (operator steps we recommend for on-call).

If you prefer, I can copy the condensed timeline into your ticketing system and trigger an executive summary for your auditors.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
irene@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Technical timeline + proposed permanent fix details (for customer-facing summary)

Irene/Hannah — below is a clear, non-jargon version we can include in the customer brief and a slightly more technical appendix for your SOC/compliance teams. Feel free to extract or shorten.

Plain-language timeline (to put in the PDF):
- 18:02 UTC — elevated queue latency observed by internal monitors; PaymentsPlus telemetry shows first 500 errors.
- 18:03–18:25 UTC — root cause analysis: we saw concurrent large sequence-length requests that pushed our KV-cache eviction policy into an aggressive path. At the same time, a recently introduced GPU driver change increased the driver's async timeout under heavy load. The combination led to a race where the runtime attempted a synchronous KV flush while the driver stalled, causing request handlers to pile up and produce 5xx responses.
- 18:25 UTC — applied temporary mitigations: reverted KV-cache aggressiveness change and applied driver runtime flag rollback to reduce async timeout back to the previous baseline.
- 18:48 UTC — error rates returned to normal and latency normalized; we kept increased monitoring for 48 hours.

Root cause (engineer-level):
- Trigger: regression in driver async timeout (driver vX.Y.Z+delta) interacting with runtime's new aggressive-KV-eviction path under pathological seqlen distributions.
- Failure mode: thread starvation on the serving runtime leading to cascading request queue buildup and token generation timeouts.

Permanent fix plan and schedule:
- Short-term (this week): release runtime v2.14.3 that adds a defensive backoff when KV eviction would coincide with driver timeouts; rollout to Dedicated pools via canary (72 hours).
- Medium-term (next week): coordinate with cloud image/kernel team to stage kernel-driver patch (patch id: KDRV-9876); we will manage a non-disruptive deployment and provide the patch notes (kernel_patch_notes.txt).
- Long-term: add a regression test that synthesizes high-seqlen tails to catch this interaction in CI. ETA Q1 2027.

Diagnostics attached: full heap/kv histograms and the minimal repro we used (in internal bucket); I recommend we mention the SUP ticket: SUP-1234 in the customer doc so they can link it to their change control.

David Kim
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Final brief + verification window for PaymentsPlus (action items enclosed)

Maria — following our internal edits and David's technical appendix, please find the final short brief attached and below is a compact action handoff so your SREs can verify closure quickly.

Summary (one paragraph):
Last-week's elevated latency and intermittent 5xxs were caused by an unfortunate interaction between a GPU driver timeout regression and an aggressive KV-cache eviction path in our serving runtime under a high-sequence-length workload. We applied timely mitigations, validated the fix in your Dedicated pool, and have a staged permanent fix plan (runtime patch this week, kernel-driver patch next week).

Requested verification window: Thu 2026-12-03 10:00–10:30 PST (we will run load tests and review logs together). Please confirm or propose an alternate 30-minute slot.

Action handoff for PaymentsPlus SRE (quick checklist):
1) Confirm pool id and host set: dedicated-pool-pp-7, hosts ppool-7-12..15 — verify no new 5xx spikes during the window.
2) Run the provided smoke script (attached in mitigation_playbook.md) to generate seqlen tail traffic for 5 minutes.
3) Share the following logs during the call: serving-runtime.log (last 60m), driver-async-stats.json, and our shared dashboard link.
4) If anything looks off, request immediate rollback via the Redwood Console route we discussed in the PDF (Ops > Rollback).

We will send the runtime canary notes to you before the deployment and keep SUP-1234 updated with all patch activities. If you need an auditor-ready extract for compliance, tell me the recipient and I'll send a redacted appendix.

Thanks — looking forward to the verification.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
irene@redwoodinference.com
